note: Updated Sat 10 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT (weekend, markets closed); one session since Friday 9 Oct's close, which itself followed Thursday's tech-led selloff. Friday was a broad risk-on rebound across every major US index: S&P 500 7,811.54 (+0.59%), Nasdaq Composite 27,366.17 (+0.64%), Dow 51,654.95 (+0.83%), Russell 2000 2,806.98 (+0.46%), VIX 14.84 (-3.70%, down from Thursday's 15.41) -- low vol falling further rather than the tech-only bounce the Thursday rotation might have suggested. The one discordant data point: preliminary UMich consumer sentiment for October printed 46.3, a five-month low, missing the 47.8 consensus and down from September's 48.1; the current-conditions sub-index fell to an all-time low (44.7) even as the expectations sub-index ticked up, and 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% -- a soft, stagflation-flavored print that nonetheless did not dent Friday's risk appetite, consistent with markets reading weak data as supportive of a Fed pause/cut path. Precious metals and broad commodities melted up alongside equities rather than acting as a risk-off hedge: gold +1.52% to $4,220.30, silver +3.46% to $61.11, GDX +2.95% to $89.28, SILJ +2.70% to $27.40 -- an unusual everything-rallies session best read as repricing toward a less-hawkish Fed path rather than genuine risk-off demand. Barrick Gold was the lone laggard in the gold complex (-2.33% to $40.69, vs NEM +1.98%), tied to company-specific 2026 production-guidance cuts (2.9-3.25Moz vs 3.26Moz produced in 2025) rather than a macro signal. Oil held near Thursday's Hormuz-driven spike without retreating or extending (WTI $91.66 +0.19%, Brent $104.43 +0.14%), so the tanker-attack supply-risk premium remains fully live. Bitcoin bounced modestly off Thursday's ~$81,845 low to $82,551.86 (+1.07%), a tentative stabilization rather than a reversal. Asia's HK/SG/JP/KR index-level closes in the price spine still lag to Thursday 8 Oct (Hang Seng -1.43%, STI -3.49%, Nikkei -1.42%, KOSPI -2.62%) even though individual HK/SG single stocks already carry Friday bars -- a feed-consolidation lag, not a fresh Friday signal, and not a holiday. MP Materials and LYC.AX again printed flat/duplicate bars with no genuine new price signal. China's rare-earth export-control truce (in place since the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi meeting) was extended 23 Sep 2026 (Bessent) from its original 10 Nov 2026 expiry to 10 Jan 2027 -- a shorter-than-hoped two-month rollover, still the next binary catalyst. No active government shutdown -- the Sept 2 continuing resolution funds the government through Dec 11, 2026.

macro.regime: Friday's broad risk-on rebound (VIX down to 14.84) offsets a weak UMich sentiment print, with the hawkish Fed and a live Hormuz oil shock still the key standing risks
macro.narrative: Friday 9 Oct was a genuine broad-based risk-on rebound after Thursday's tech-led selloff: all four major US indices rose together (S&P +0.59%, Nasdaq +0.64%, Dow +0.83%, Russell +0.46%) and VIX fell a further 3.70% to 14.84, erasing Thursday's duration-driven rotation rather than extending it. The one genuinely discordant input was preliminary UMich consumer sentiment, which printed 46.3 -- a five-month low, missing the 47.8 consensus and down from 48.1 in September -- with the current-conditions sub-index collapsing to an all-time low (44.7) and 1-year inflation expectations rising to 4.7%; markets appear to be reading this soft, stagflation-flavored print as supportive of a less-hawkish Fed path rather than as a growth scare, which helps explain why equities, gold, and silver all rallied together Friday instead of gold acting as a risk-off hedge (gold +1.52%, silver +3.46%, GDX +2.95%). The confirmed hawkish Sept FOMC dot plot (19-0 hike, 16 of 18 eyeing one more 2026 hike) and the prior weak 30-year auction tail (5.31%/2.6bp) remain unresolved structural headwinds for duration even as near-term risk appetite improved. Oil held its Hormuz-driven spike without retreating (WTI $91.66, Brent $104.43, both roughly flat on the day), so the tanker-attack supply-risk premium is still fully live, not fading. Bitcoin's modest bounce (+1.07% to $82,551.86) off Thursday's low looks like tentative stabilization rather than a trend reversal. Barrick Gold's -2.33% divergence from the rest of the mining complex (NEM +1.98%) was idiosyncratic, tied to a 2026 production-guidance cut, not a read on the metals thesis. China's rare-earth export-control truce, originally set to expire 10 Nov 2026 from the Oct 2025 Busan summit, was extended a further two months to 10 Jan 2027 by a 23 Sep 2026 Bessent announcement around the Trump-Xi Washington summit -- shorter than the six-month-to-two-year extension markets had hoped for, so it remains a live but now slightly more distant binary catalyst. Asia's index-level closes in the price spine still lag to Thursday, so the region's read-through to Friday's rebound is not yet confirmed.
